tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest disk to the target, and finally move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have a clean, ordered stack of disks on a peg and need to transfer the whole stack to another peg while preserving order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain on the source peg, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, check that the disk being moved is the topmost disk on its source peg and that placing it on the destination peg does not put a larger disk on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every move you generate, perform these two checks to avoid illegal configurations.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a disk that is buried under other disks, or placing a larger disk onto a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you want to move has smaller disks stacked above it, first relocate those smaller disks to other pegs so the target disk becomes topmost.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not currently the top disk on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 2 sits on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it ideal for temporarily holding other disks while larger moves are performed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg to hold a disk temporarily, move the smallest disk there first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk onto a peg that already has a smaller disk, without first moving the smallest disk away.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target blocking disk before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg has a smaller disk on top, move that smaller disk elsewhere before moving the larger disk onto the peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the top of the target peg is smaller than the disk you intend to place there.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 1 is on top, causing a size violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the target peg already contains some of the final stack’s larger disks in correct order, treat that stack as a fixed base and only add smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When building the final tower and the target peg already has correctly placed larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place a smaller disk beneath an already placed larger disk, breaking the order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear auxiliary peg of smaller disks before using it for larger moves
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a peg is needed as the auxiliary (or source) for moving larger disks, ensure that any smaller disks on that peg are moved elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before using a peg as a temporary holder for larger disks, verify it contains no smaller disks that would block the move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Using a peg that still holds disk 1 as the auxiliary while trying to move disk 3 onto it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When assembling the final tower from an arbitrary initial distribution, handle disks from largest to smallest, moving each to its final position after clearing any obstacles.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal is to build a complete stack on a target peg and the initial configuration is scattered.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving smaller disks before placing the largest disk, resulting in the largest disk being blocked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear all smaller disks from target peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto the target peg, relocate every smaller disk currently on that peg (starting from the top) to other pegs, ensuring the target peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the target peg contains any disks smaller than the disk you intend to move onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 onto a peg that still has disks 3 and 1, causing a size ordering violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the complete sequence of moves, output it as the last list in the response (e.g., 'moves = [[...]]' or just the list), with no additional list‑like text after it, so the scorer can correctly parse the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very end of the answer, before any concluding remarks or extra text.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing extra text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the moves and reject the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves, often after a reasoning paragraph.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate the full move list, even if it is long; verify that the list appears before ending the response.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on reaching the goal without checking the size rule for the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, confirm that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on its goal position without verifying its accessibility.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before committing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Generation is cut off by the token limit or by an early stop token, leaving the move sequence unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the move sequence ahead of time and ensure the entire list fits within the response length; if necessary, split into multiple short moves but keep the list syntactically complete.
